# Version 1.2.0 (October 28, 2026)
![Number of release downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/JanusGraph/janusgraph/v1.2.0/total.svg)

Full documentation can be found at https://docs.janusgraph.org/

```xml
<dependency>
   <groupId>org.janusgraph</groupId>
   <artifactId>janusgraph-core</artifactId>
   <version>1.2.0</version>
</dependency>
```

For more information on features and bug fixes in 1.2.0, see [this GitHub milestone](https://github.com/JanusGraph/janusgraph/milestone/30?closed=1).

Upgrade instructions are provided in the changelog of the release: https://docs.janusgraph.org/master/changelog/#upgrade-instructions

## Notable new features

- Upgrade to Apache TinkerPop 3.8.2 (breaking: TinkerPop 3.8 changes Gremlin semantics, see the upgrade instructions)
- Java 11 is now the minimum supported Java version (support for Java 8 is dropped); added support for Java 17, 21 and 25
- Support for Apache Cassandra 5.0. The pre-packaged distribution now bundles Cassandra 5.0.9
- CQL storage backend transitioned from the DataStax Java Driver to the Apache Cassandra Java Driver
- Support for Elasticsearch 9
- Support for OpenSearch 2 and 3 through the `elasticsearch` index backend
- Support for Solr 9 (Solr 8 is deprecated) and upgrade to Apache Lucene 9
- Elasticsearch 6.0 is no longer supported (Elasticsearch 6.1 and newer still are)
- CDC-based mixed index synchronization: mixed indexes can be kept eventually consistent with the graph through Cassandra Change-Data-Capture and the new `janusgraph-cdc` worker (opt-in)
- New `WRITE_ONLY_ENABLED` index state: reindex an index without enabling it, or stop using an enabled index for queries while it keeps receiving updates
- New `REMOVE_STALE_ENTRIES` schema action to remove the entries of deleted elements from composite and mixed indexes
- Reindex a given subset of vertices instead of scanning the whole graph (CQL)
- Management APIs that decode vertex ids and composite index keys from their hex strings, for debugging
- Optional automatic closing of unreachable (zombie) instances during index status updates
- Recurring transaction recovery and failure statistics for transaction recovery
- Ordering by `LIST` properties through a mixed index
- `textContainsPhrase` support for Solr
- Much faster mixed index reindex and OLAP scans: batched document restores, signal-based row hand-off between scan threads, opt-in parallel token-range scans, a scan-only page size and `PER PARTITION LIMIT` pushdown for CQL, and scan progress logging
- Removing a vertex deletes its whole storage row in one operation, which drastically reduces tombstones when removing super-nodes on CQL
- Ordered traversals such as `g.V().order().by('name').limit(10)` are answered by a mixed index which holds the order keys; orders which the index backend can't sort by are sorted by JanusGraph
- Faster reads of large index results: Elasticsearch point-in-time paging (adaptive by default), scroll contexts only for results larger than a page, larger pages for limited results beyond 10,000 hits, and Solr results read in growing pages
- More resilient Elasticsearch backend: transient read and write failures are retried by default instead of failing the traversal or dropping the index mutation, missing documents are recreated whole, configurable connection pool (up to 30 connections to a single host) and lighter bulk requests
- The Gremlin pool of JanusGraph Server can run on virtual threads (Java 24 and newer)
- Core and storage performance improvements: relations without properties are parsed once, composite index lookups of several values read their index rows together, CQL reads more properties of a vertex per query and marks its write batches idempotent, ID blocks of different partitions are claimed in parallel, lock-free sampling of metrics
- A graph runs its background work on fewer, bounded threads which end when the graph closes
- BerkeleyJE now enforces `LOCK` co

detail.readme:
[![JanusGraph logo](janusgraph.png)](https://janusgraph.org/)

JanusGraph is a highly scalable [graph database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_database)
optimized for storing and querying large graphs with billions of vertices and edges
distributed across a multi-machine cluster. JanusGraph is a transactional database that
can support thousands of concurrent users, complex traversals, and analytic graph queries.

## Learn More

The [project homepage](https://janusgraph.org) contains more information on JanusGraph and
provides links to documentation, getting-started guides and release downloads.

## Visualization

JanusGraph has a web-based graph visualizer located in [janusgraph-visualizer](https://github.com/JanusGraph/janusgraph-visualizer) 
repository. 

In additional to the web-based graph visualizer, JanusGraph supports a range of third party graph visualizers listed below:

* [Arcade Analytics](https://arcadeanalytics.com/usermanual/#arcade-analytics)
* [Cytoscape](https://www.cytoscape.org/)
* [Gephi](https://tinkerpop.apache.org/docs/current/reference/#gephi-plugin)
  plugin for Apache TinkerPop
* [Graphexp](https://github.com/bricaud/graphexp)
* [Graph Explorer](https://github.com/invanalabs/graph-explorer)
* [Graphlytic](https://graphlytic.com/)
* [Gremlin-Visualizer](https://github.com/prabushitha/gremlin-visualizer) - the original repository on which [JanusGraph-Visualizer](https://github.com/JanusGraph/janusgraph-visualizer) is based on.
* [G.V() - Gremlin IDE](https://gdotv.com)
* [KeyLines by Cambridge Intelligence](https://cambridge-intelligence.com/keylines/janusgraph/)
* [Ogma by Linkurious](https://doc.linkurious.com/ogma/latest/tutorials/janusgraph/)
* [ReGraph by Cambridge Intelligence](https://cambridge-intelligence.com/regraph/)
* [Tom Sawyer Perspectives](https://www.tomsawyer.com/perspectives/)

## Community

* GitHub Discussions: see [`GitHub Discussions`](https://github.com/JanusGraph/janusgraph/discussions)
  for all general discussions and questions about JanusGraph

* Discord for interactive discussions and questions about JanusGraph: [Join the server](https://discord.gg/5n4fjv4QAf)

* Stack Overflow: see the
  [`janusgraph`](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/janusgraph) tag

* Twitter: follow [@JanusGraph](https://twitter.com/JanusGraph) for news and
  updates

* LinkedIn: follow [JanusGraph](https://www.linkedin.com/company/janusgraph) for news and
  updates

* Mailing lists:

  * **janusgraph-users (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation**
    ([archives](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-users/topics))
    for questions about using JanusGraph, installation, configuration, integrations

    To join with a LF AI & Data account, use the [web
    UI](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-users/join); to
    subscribe/unsubscribe with an arbitrary email address, send an email to:

    * janusgraph-users+subscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation
    * janusgraph-users+unsubscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation

  * **janusgraph-dev (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation**
    ([archives](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-dev/topics))
    for internal implementation of JanusGraph itself

    To join with a LF AI & Data account, use the [web
    UI](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-dev/join); to
    subscribe/unsubscribe with an arbitrary email address, send an email to:

    * janusgraph-dev+subscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation
    * janusgraph-dev+unsubscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation

  * **janusgraph-announce (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation**
    ([archives](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-announce/topics))
    for new releases and news announcements

    To join with a LF AI & Data account, use the [web
    UI](https://lists.lfaidata.foundation/g/janusgraph-announce/join); to
    subscribe/unsubscribe with an arbitrary email address, send an email to:

    * janusgraph-announce+subscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation
    * janusgraph-announce+unsubscribe (at) lists.lfaidata.foundation

CLAs and best practices for working with GitHub.

* [Open Network Automation Platform (ONAP)](https://www.onap.org/) - automation and orchestration for Software-Defined Networks
- [Uber Knowledge Graph](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C01Gh0g01JE) ([event info](https://leap.ai/events/2017/08/06/uber_knowledge_graph))

* [Windup](https://github.com/windup/windup) by RedHat - application migration and assessment tool ([website](https://developers.redhat.com/products/rhamt/overview/))
